tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Ask the person for their yes to one call, on a card they tap. Some calls need the person's yes before they run: when a call comes back needing it, ask with this call, with the same capability and arguments, and never with a question in words. Explain in why what the call does and the arguments that matter. The person answers on the card, Approve or Deny; a yes written in a conversation approves nothing. A yes runs nothing: it grants a ticket, which run_approved runs once. Never approve on anyone's behalf. There is no other way to get a yes. Comes back saying the request was written and waits on the person, that the hub page's approvals panel shows it, and how its card went on the line; or, writing nothing, why not: the call is not one you are offered or its arguments do not fit, it is not allowed and is not to be asked about, or the same request already waits on the person, and since when.

tools.name: spawn
tools.description: Set up work that runs later or separately: a scheduled task, which starts an activation of its own when it falls due, reading what it carries. Spawn only work that runs later or separately. Give at most one of at, delay_minutes, after and rule; with none it falls due now. A task suggests only places on your place list. A task you were shown by its T label is replaced by one spawn naming it in replaces; find any other with list_tasks first. "Snooze 10 minutes" or "again tomorrow", after a task's message, is a new spawn: a one-off task with the same instruction, written from what you were shown of the episode that wrote the message, suggesting the place the person said it in. Skipping a rule's next occurrence ("skip tomorrow's") is a spawn replacing it with the same rule from the local date after the skipped one, or its cancel where none would follow before its until. "Tomorrow at 9 instead" is that skip and a one-off task at the new time, in the same round. Write a local time with no UTC offset unless the person named one, and give a zone only where the person named one. Say a task back from its read_back, never from your own reckoning of the time. Where the words could mean more than one task, ask which.
